run_dispatcher.description: Whether to run the networkd-dispatcher service at all. Set to false to disable.

items.description: Absolute path to a directory containing state scripts (e.g., up.d/, down.d/)

script_dirs.description: Colon-separated list of directories to search for state scripts. First match wins for script execution.

log_level.description: Minimum log level. Logs below this level are suppressed.

log_to_journal.description: Enable logging to systemd journal. Recommended for production.

log_to_file.description: Enable logging to a file. Requires a valid `log_dir`.

log_dir.description: Directory where log files are written if `log_to_file` is enabled.

log_to_stdout.description: Enable logging to standard output. Useful for debugging or containerized deployments.

script_timeout.description: Maximum time (in seconds) a script may run before being forcefully terminated.

fail_on_script_error.description: If true, the dispatcher exits with a non-zero code if any script fails. If false, script failures are logged but ignored.

items.description: Interface name to monitor (e.g., eth0, wlan0). Empty means all interfaces.

monitored_interfaces.description: If non-empty, only events for listed interfaces are processed. Supports wildcards via regex in `excluded_interfaces_regex`.

items.description: Regex pattern to exclude matching interfaces.

excluded_interfaces_regex.description: Space-separated list of regex patterns. Any interface matching a pattern is skipped.

allow_root_scripts.description: If true, allow scripts to run as root. ⚠️ Security warning: Only enable if scripts are trusted and need elevated privileges.

runtime_dir.description: Directory for runtime state (locks, PID, temp files). Should be on tmpfs for ephemeral systems.

items.description: Environment variable assignment in KEY=VALUE format (e.g., MY_VAR=foo).

extra_env_vars.description: Additional environment variables exposed to all scripts.

event_filter.description: Enable or disable specific event types. Keys are lowercase event names (e.g., up, down, dhcp, dns). Values are booleans or missing (no change).
